title: the-domain-carries-the-inference-side
intention: The second part of the inference proxy: domain verticals (coding, research, general-as-default) berthed as authored rows beside the rules stacks, carrying the domain-specific aspects of GETTING an inference — escalation handler, prompts, and (when a consumer pulls them) agentic helpers — so a calling device names its domain and the request arrives dressed, with the reasoning staying in the caller. The librarian holds the first research-domain instance.
why: Akien, 2026-08-08: 'now there was supposed to be a second part to the inference proxy. domains.' The rules stack that closed yesterday answers WHERE and at-what-cost an inference runs; nothing yet answers WITH WHAT CONTENT a request arrives — every request crosses the sole path naked, and the escalate-to-LLM pattern the idea names is already built three separate times unberthed (orient.deepen's failover, learning_block's decide-or-escalate, learning/'s tiered recall), each caller re-deriving what a domain would answer once (Law 1). The lived symptom nearest to hand: the librarian's chat turn — live on Hex at 4.0s since yesterday — has nowhere to say 'this is research'; any research-shaped behavior would be hand-built prompt scaffolding at the call site.
traces_to: Telos 1 (a domain's prompts and escalation policy answered once and compiled into structure per vertical, not re-derived per caller — Law 1); Law 6 (one owner: domain-specific inference aspects get one address behind inference_domain's gate instead of accreting per-caller); Telos 2 rides it (the librarian as first research-domain consumer).

falsifier.proves_green: code-seam@v2's registered set: entry gate at the BUILDME forward crossing (cast ticket + intent_berth + sorted_berth + berthed chart chain claiming this ticket); build gate at the PROVEME forward crossing (build_inspector's nest over cairn/devices/inference_domain, including sole_path_holds and the gradation sieves); emission gate at the WATCHME forward crossing (probe berthed at cairn/devices/inference_domain/probes/does_a_domain_ride_the_request.py, importable, module-level PROBE with carry and enough, armed before the crossing); exit gate at the PROVED entry (verdict artifact answering the claiming validate berth's criteria by their instruments); proof gate: plain-python teeth beside the code under the tester (netns seal), the standing test_inference_domain.py + test_host.py + test_route.py suites green through the change.
falsifier.proves_red: RED on any of: (1) a caller names a domain and the request arrives without that domain's prompts/escalation actually applied (domains decorative — the 'stacks exist but a literal decides' defect one seam up); (2) the librarian's real chat turn cannot ride a research domain; (3) a bare call breaks or behaves differently than before the build (general is not actually the default); (4) domain logic branches per caller inside inference_domain (the boundary sentence breached — reasoning leaked out of the calling device); (5) every consumer mints its own bespoke domain (the vertical is not real — per-device config wearing a class name); (6) a device wants to compose aspects across two domains (domains are FIELD SETS an instance composes, not classes it belongs to — the ticket/probe/task precedent — and the shape must dissolve).
falsifier.horizon: Re-read at: the first non-librarian consumer (an inspector failing over to LLM with learning — those tickets cast when the consumer appears, per the idea's own 'could result in tickets'); the first appearance of a subclass need ('different kinds of research' — does it compose rows or demand a hierarchy?); any resurfacing of the domain-naming distinction (recorded in the sorted berth's collision check: ownership-sense vs subject-sense, disambiguated by address, standing for Akien's overrule).
